extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners / attorneys admitted to practice before the USPTO (respondents in disciplinary proceedings)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing professional conduct, sanctions, and reinstatement for attorneys/agents practicing before the United States Patent and Trademark Office under the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and related regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is an attorney registered to practice patent law before the Office (Registration Number ...) and is subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26. Being registered to practice before the Office makes a practitioner subject to the USPTO disciplinary rules and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a) — consent after full disclosure where independent judgment may be affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation: accepting employment from PTI without the consent of the PTI-referred client after full disclosure where the exercise of Respondent's independent professional judgment on behalf of the referred client will be or reasonably may be affected by the practitioner's own financial, business, property, or personal interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facts: Respondent accepted referrals and compensation from PTI and did not disclose the specific amount received nor obtain clients' consent after full disclosure. Applies where a practitioner's business relationship could reasonably affect independent professional judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.66(a) and 10.66(b) — conflicts/multiple clients and declining employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation: not declining employment from PTI and representing multiple clients where the exercise of Respondent's independent professional judgment on behalf of a client will be or is likely to be adversely affected by the acceptance of the proffered employment or if it would be likely to involve Respondent in representing differing interests and where it is obvious that Respondent cannot adequately represent the interest of each, without first obtaining the consent of each client to the representation after full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facts: Respondent represented numerous PTI-referred clients under arrangements that raised potential conflicts; the rule requires declining or obtaining informed consent when multiple representations or other circumstances would adversely affect independent judgment or create differing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1) — accepting compensation from a third party without client consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation: accepting compensation from PTI for Respondent's legal services to the PTI-referred client without the consent of the PTI-referred client after full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facts: Respondent received payment from PTI (a third party) for work on referred clients but did not disclose that compensation or obtain the referred clients' consent after full disclosure. The rule prohibits third-party payment without client consent when it may affect the practitioner's independent judgment or create conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(4) — prompt payment/return of unearned advance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation: not promptly paying to the PTI-referred clients that portion of advance fees for patent legal services not yet completed by Respondent and to which the PTI-referred clients were entitled to receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facts: PTI paid Respondent in advance to prepare and file patent applications; after PTI entered receivership Respondent neither filed the applications nor returned the unearned portion of the fees. Practitioners must promptly account for and return unearned advance fees to clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose potential conflicts and obtain informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must disclose business relationships and potential conflicts and obtain the client's consent after full disclosure before accepting representation or compensation that may affect independent professional judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by Respondent's failure to disclose the specific amount he received from PTI, failure to obtain consent after full disclosure, and failure to disclose potential conflicts arising from his business relationship with PTI prior to representing PTI-referred clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension and limited recognition to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for sixty (60) months from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO; Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring ninety (90) days after the date the Final Order is signed, solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b), including responding only to outstanding office actions received on or before the date the Final Order is signed (e.g., paying issue fees, filing petitions for revival).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifies both the principal sanction (60-month suspension) and a short, narrowly-limited recognition period to permit winding up specified outstanding matters; limited recognition is strictly constrained to specified actions and time frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (requirements applicable to suspended practitioners) for the full period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance includes duties set forth in § 11.58 (e.g., notification, handling of client matters) and is an explicit condition to eligibility for reinstatement and other relief described in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to remove name from third-party USPTO customer numbers and provide proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Within ninety (90) days from the date the Final Order is signed, Respondent shall contact the law firms holding specified USPTO Customer Numbers and request in writing that each law firm take steps to remove Respondent's name from its USPTO Customer Number; within one hundred and twenty (120) days Respondent shall provide the OED Director with an affidavit and corroborating documents (e.g., the written requests) establishing that the requests were made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific customer numbers are listed; practitioner must take affirmative steps and provide documentary proof of removal requests within the timeframes set by the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of Respondent from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from Customer Number 52,123 and the public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificate associated with Customer Number 52,123.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent may apply for and obtain a USPTO Customer Number in his own name provided it is used solely for representing himself as the sole inventor; Respondent may not obtain a USPTO customer number or PKI certificate for the purpose of representing others before the Office unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition requirements under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 and § 11.7
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement after eighteen (18) months from the date the Final Order is signed requesting reinstatement effective prior to the expiration of the 60-month suspension; reinstatement requires proof satisfying 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c) that (1) Respondent has the good moral character and reputation, competency, and learning in law required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7 for admission, (2) resumption of practice will not be detrimental to the administration of justice or subversive to the public interest, (3) Respondent has complied with the provisions of the Final Order for the full period of suspension, and (4) Respondent has complied with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 for the full period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order makes eligibility to seek reinstatement contingent on meeting regulatory standards of character and competence and full compliance with the disciplinary order and suspension obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director authority: Order to Show Cause and amendment/lifting of stay for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply during the 60-month period, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause (with procedures depending on whether Respondent has been reinstated or not), send it to Respondent's last address, grant fifteen (15) days to respond, and after consideration may deliver the matter to the USPTO Director to amend the Final Order (e.g., delay reinstatement eligibility to 60 months or lift a stay and reinstate suspension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure includes issuing the Order to Show Cause, 15-day response period, transmission of the Order and evidence to the USPTO Director, and possible outcomes (amend Final Order, lift stay, immediate suspension of remaining period). These are enforcement mechanisms for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements (Reading Room, Official Gazette, and disciplinary agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (with application numbers and third-party names redacted); the OED Director shall publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; and pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes a sample Notice of Suspension text and specifies redaction of third-party names and application numbers; dissemination is mandatory and broad (Reading Room, Official Gazette, state disciplinary agencies, courts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct brought to the Office's attention, and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding (a) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or (b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order is to be treated as precedent/consideration material in future matters involving the same practitioner and may aggravate or rebut claims in later proceedings.
